text: Castellan Specialty Insurance has acquired Thornbury Underwriting Partners, and the combined company will operate under the Castellan name. This lab walks through designing the identity architecture for that merger — a real decision a security engineer has to make, not just vocabulary.

Castellan runs 2,400 employees on Microsoft Entra ID, with Conditional Access enforced org-wide, standard users on Authenticator push, and FIDO2 hardware keys required for admins. Thornbury runs 380 employees on Okta, with no Conditional Access at all and sixty percent of users still authenticating with SMS one-time codes — the weakest common MFA factor. Day one, every Thornbury employee still needs to get their work done, merger or not.

The team federates first instead of migrating everything immediately. Entra ID becomes the surviving identity plane, Okta keeps brokering Thornbury's roughly forty apps during the transition, and each app migrates on its own schedule over two quarters. Okta is decommissioned only once the last app has cut over.

App by app, the standard in use dictates the work. PolicyTrack only supports SAML 2.0, so it needs a new entity ID and ACS URL before Okta's signing certificate expires in seven months. ClaimLine uses OIDC and needs a new client ID and redirect URI, with Okta kept as a short-term broker for contract reasons.

MFA rolls out in three phases, not one switch, because the two companies didn't start from the same place. Phase one, thirty days: a pilot group of Thornbury's own IT team moves to Authenticator push under a report-only Conditional Access policy that logs what it would block without blocking anything yet. Phase two, ninety days: every remaining Thornbury standard user is cut over, and SMS is disabled as a registered method once that's confirmed. Phase three, one hundred twenty days: Thornbury admins reach the same FIDO2 hardware-key bar Castellan's admins already clear.

Identity is federated, the app migration order is set, and MFA has a real timeline accounting for where each company actually started. Next up: building and rolling out the hardening baseline the newly combined Windows and Linux fleet still needs.
